## Natural history notes

A tiny casebearer moth characterized by narrow, plain brownish to grayish wings as an adult, though it is more often recognized by the larval case carried on its host plant. In Florida, it is associated with yellow-eyed grasses in the genus Xyris, especially in wet meadows, marsh edges, pine flatwoods, and other open, seasonally moist habitats where these plants grow. The larvae feed on Xyris seed heads from within a portable silken case, while adults are small, delicate moths that may be overlooked unless swept from vegetation or attracted to lights.
